impact: Less severe for the memory chain than first feared: Korea and Taiwan sit in the capped 15% tier and chips may be exempt, which eases the hit to MU, DRAM, SNXX and SKM's home market. China remains the main target.
summary: USTR Jamieson Greer on November 25 proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners after an eight-month probe into excess industrial capacity: China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the EU, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. China faces a 20% rate stacked on the 25% 2018 tariffs, which could rise to 40% without a favorable deal, with an exemption proposed for about $30 billion of Chinese goods. Update Nov 26: rates for the EU, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan are capped at 15% under existing trade deals, and one report says semiconductors and other high-tech goods from Taiwan and Korea are proposed for exemption. China's foreign ministry called the rationale a false issue, but analysts expect no countermeasures. With a comment period and hearings, nothing takes effect before January 2027 at the earliest.
title: US proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 partners; China faces extra 20%
